262:     /// Attempt to do a fast confirmation of a word match that covers a subset
263:     /// (but hopefully a big subset) of most cases. Ok(Some(..)) is returned
264:     /// when a match is found. Ok(None) is returned when there is definitively
265:     /// no match. Err(()) is returned when this routine could not detect
266:     /// whether there was a match or not.
267:     fn fast_find(
268:         &self,
269:         haystack: &[u8],
270:         at: usize,
271:     ) -> Result<Option<Match>, ()> {
272:         // This is a bit hairy. The whole point here is to avoid running a
273:         // slower regex engine to extract capture groups. Remember, our word
274:         // regex looks like this:
275:         //
276:         //     (^|\W)(<original regex>)(\W|$)
277:         //
278:         // What we want are the match offsets of <original regex>. So in the
279:         // easy/common case, the original regex will be sandwiched between
280:         // two codepoints that are in the \W class. So our approach here is to
281:         // look for a match of the overall word regexp, strip the \W ends and
282:         // then check whether the original regex matches what's left. If so,
283:         // then we are guaranteed a correct match.
284:         //
285:         // This only works though if we know that the match is sandwiched
286:         // between two \W codepoints. This only occurs when neither ^ nor $
287:         // match. This in turn only occurs when the match is at either the
288:         // beginning or end of the haystack. In either of those cases, we
289:         // declare defeat and defer to the slower implementation.
290:         //
291:         // The reason why we cannot handle the ^/$ cases here is because we
292:         // can't assume anything about the original pattern. (Try commenting
293:         // out the checks for ^/$ below and run the tests to see examples.)
294:         let input = Input::new(haystack).span(at..haystack.len());
295:         let mut cand = match self.regex.find(input) {
296:             None => return Ok(None),
297:             Some(m) => Match::new(m.start(), m.end()),
298:         };
299:         if cand.start() == 0 || cand.end() == haystack.len() {
300:             return Err(());
301:         }
302:         let (_, slen) = bstr::decode_utf8(&haystack[cand]);
303:         let (_, elen) = bstr::decode_last_utf8(&haystack[cand]);
304:         let new_start = cand.start() + slen;
305:         let new_end = cand.end() - elen;
306:         // This occurs the original regex can match the empty string. In this
307:         // case, just bail instead of trying to get it right here since it's
308:         // likely a pathological case.
309:         if new_start > new_end {
310:             return Err(());
311:         }
312:         cand = cand.with_start(new_start).with_end(new_end);
313:         if self.original.is_match(&haystack[cand]) {
314:             Ok(Some(cand))
315:         } else {
316:             Err(())
317:         }
318:     }
319: }

403:     pub(crate) fn wrap_hir_with_word_boundary(
404:         chir: ConfiguredHIR,
405:     ) -> Result<ConfiguredHIR, Error> {
406:         let non_word = {
407:             let mut config = chir.config().clone();
408:             config.fixed_strings = false;
409:             ConfiguredHIR::new(config, &[r"\W"])?
410:         };
411:         let line_anchor_start = Hir::look(Self::line_anchor_start_for(chir.config()));
412:         let line_anchor_end = Hir::look(Self::line_anchor_end_for(chir.config()));
413:         let wrapped = Hir::concat(vec![
414:             Hir::alternation(vec![line_anchor_start, non_word.hir().clone()]),
415:             Hir::capture(hir::Capture {
416:                 index: 1,
417:                 name: None,
418:                 sub: Box::new(Self::renumber_capture_indices(chir.hir().clone())?),
419:             }),
420:             Hir::alternation(vec![non_word.hir().clone(), line_anchor_end]),
421:         ]);
422:         Ok(ConfiguredHIR::from_parts(chir.config().clone(), wrapped))
423:     }

441:     pub(crate) fn renumber_capture_indices(hir: Hir) -> Result<Hir, Error> {
442:         Ok(match hir.into_kind() {
443:             HirKind::Empty => Hir::empty(),
444:             HirKind::Literal(hir::Literal(lit)) => Hir::literal(lit),
445:             HirKind::Class(cls) => Hir::class(cls),
446:             HirKind::Look(x) => Hir::look(x),
447:             HirKind::Repetition(mut x) => {
448:                 x.sub = Box::new(Self::renumber_capture_indices(*x.sub)?);
449:                 Hir::repetition(x)
450:             }
451:             HirKind::Capture(mut cap) => {
452:                 cap.index = match cap.index.checked_add(1) {
453:                     Some(index) => index,
454:                     None => {

456:                         return Err(Error::any(msg));

458:                 };
459:                 cap.sub = Box::new(Self::renumber_capture_indices(*cap.sub)?);

part.text:
Implemented the `--word-regexp` correction in `crates/regex/src/word.rs`.

- Replaced the consuming `(?:^|\W)(pattern)(?:$|\W)` wrapper with true zero-width `\b(pattern)\b` boundaries, matching the documented behavior.
- Removed the delimiter-stripping fast path, which relied on consuming surrounding non-word characters and caused the incorrect `ome.domain.com` match.
- Added a regression test for issue 2576 covering both normal and capture-based matching paths.
- Verified formatting with `git diff --check`.

Test execution was blocked because the required Docker container has no `cargo`, `rustc`, or `rg` executable on `PATH`.
